pr_title: [WIP] X509: Refactor X509_PUBKEY processing to include provider side keys
pr_body:
When a SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) is decoded into an X509_PUBKEY
structure, the corresponding EVP_PKEY is automatically added as well.
This used to only support our built-in keytypes, and only in legacy
form.

This is now refactored to try to decode the whole SPKI into an
EVP_PKEY using OSSL_DECODER, and cache that in the X509_PUBKEY very
early.  Only when that fails, the existing decoder callback will try
to create a legacy EVP_PKEY.

For purposes where it's not desirable to do the provider side SPKI
decoding, there is now a function d2i_PUBKEY_legacy().  This is used
by all the type specific d2i_<TYPE>_PUBKEY(), as well as in out
provider DER->key decoder, to avoid running into recursion problems.

Fixes #13893

-----

This includes refactoring the DER-\>key decoder to be a bit more flexible with how it uses keytype specific d2i functions and adds the possibility to use d2i_*TYPE*_PUBKEY.

This also includes the addition of SM2 encoders and decoders...
pr_comments:
Something to be noted is the inherent problem with the early caching of an EVP_PKEY in the X509_PUBKEY, when someone else wants an easy way to decode the DER, as part of a decoder implementation for a keytype we know nothing about.  It becomes a recursion problem.

The solution I could come up with was to have a `d2i_PUBKEY_legacy()`, which is currently internal.  However, that doesn't help anyone making an external provider for a keytype that's unknown to us, and that merely wants to decode the SubjectPublicKeyInfo into its parts, but no further processing (i.e. no automatic caching of an EVP_PKEY).

A slightly different solution could have been to let `x509_public_decode()` handle the decoding via OSSL_DECODER.  The only issue there is that keytypes like RSA-PSS would be a bit problematic, as its parameters aren't included in the pubkey BIT STRING itself, but rather in the AlgorithmID (X509_ALGOR) that sits beside it.

This could be resolved by decoding the X509_ALGOR `parameters` field and the X509_PUBKEY `pubkey` fields separately, which is possible with the help of d2i_*TYPE*PublicKey() and d2i_*TYPE*params(), assign what we get to EVP_PKEYs, and use EVP_PKEY_copy_parameters() to copy the parameters extracted from the X509_ALGOR onto the EVP_PKEY that contains the key itself...  the only issue there being we don't have  d2i_*TYPE*PublicKey() and d2i_*TYPE*params() for all our legacy keytypes.
Yeah, something is off. See the CI failures
What key type was there in that certificate?  I just found a problem where RSA and RSA-PSS gets mixed up...
RSA

In other words, provider backed EVP_PKEYs were *completely inaccessible* when decoding an X509_PUBKEY before this change, i.e. other algos than our built in ones were impossible.

If it is not provider backed, will it be automatically imported to provider if you do for example signature verification of a certificate with the X509_PUBKEY? IMO if that's the case, I think we can keep that.

It remains unclear to me why we would do things differently for key types that happen to have a legacy implementation vs for those that don't. If we've got the codepaths to handle provider based keys - why wouldn't we always do that if there is a provider available to do it?

Yes, this was implemented early.  The keys are exported to the provider that is to do the signature work if that provider doesn't match the key's provider (or that the key is legacy).  This is among the earliest things we implemented.

The main problem here was that if the algorithm given by the AlgorithmID *isn't known by OpenSSL*, then `X509_get_pubkey()` would obviously return NULL...  was it not?

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a2a5506b9329b978a2a5b11a518b9789446ad310/include/openssl/asn1t.h.in#L63-L66

Using that form allows a programmatic "take-over" of the processing of an item.  X509_NAME is processed this way, and it seems like the solution for our problem here is to do the same for X509_PUBKEY...

issue_context.title: Public keys decoded from an X509 certificate are legacy keys
issue_context.body:
When we decode an X509 certificate, the public key contained within it is decoded by the internal function `x509_pubkey_decode`:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/47b784a41b729d5df9ad47c99355db2f2026a709/crypto/x509/x_pubkey.c#L181-L214

This firstly takes the algorithm and uses `OBJ_obj2nid` to find a nid for it. This is the first problem. What if the algorithm comes from a provider and we don't have a nid for that algorithm? Once we have the nid we call `EVP_PKEY_set_type` which has the effect of setting the ameth on the EVP_PKEY. Subsequently we then call `ameth->pub_decode` to decode it - which obviously gives us a legacy key.

Instead we somehow need to find a decoder from a provider that is associated with the algorithm OID and use that (perhaps using "capabilities"?). Once we have the decoder we can use that to create a provider side key.
comments: @baentsch - I think this is directly relevant to the what you are trying to do.

> I think this is directly relevant to the what you are trying to do.

It is. Another spot (didn't hit on that one yet, so thanks for the heads-up) adding to several places where I found fixed tables I'm unsure how to "open up" for provider-populated sig data structures :-/

I have avoided diving too deep into X509 with regards to keys. I made an attempt once early, and found a number of unsavory corner cases... they had me back away.

The idea was anyway that legacy keys should be possible to use, and I'm not familiar with @baentsch' problem, so can't really say.

It looks, however, like we're having a trend shift toward trying our utmost to have provider side keys everywhere. That's additional time before getting to beta1...

Speaking of OIDs, an idea is to make them part of the name string.

"BLARGH:1.2.3.4"

Why complicate things further?

> The idea was anyway that legacy keys should be possible to use, and I'm not familiar with @baentsch' problem, so can't really say.

@baentsch is writing a provider for algorithms that we don't currently have in OpenSSL. Those include signature algorithms that need to be present in X509 certs.

> Speaking of OIDs, an idea is to make them part of the name string.

You mean as an alias for the usual name? Hmm...that might work.

> You mean as an alias for the usual name? Hmm...that might work.

Exactly. After all, and OID is conceptually just another identifier, or name, albeit numeric.

A provider could register the OID with OBJ_create() and get an
NID, I don't see that part as being a problem.

> A provider could register the OID with OBJ_create() and get an
NID, I don't see that part as being a problem.

That would require the provider to be linked against libcrypto which might not be the case...unless we were to make OBJ_create() an upcall, which could work. But that doesn't help us to associate the nid with the provider.

> I'm unsure how to "open up" for provider-populated sig data structures :-/

I'm not sure what the problem is that you're trying to fix. You
can create your own ASN.1 structures. If you need help, it's
probably best to open an other issue for that.

I really don't see why a provider should go through OBJ_create, or why the application (or libcrypto) should have to use yet another way to fetch an algorithm via an OID. How about this?

EVP_CIPHER_fetch(NULL, "1.2.3.4", NULL) 

OBJ_obj2txt() can help convert an ASN1_OBJECT to a numeric string where needed.
I finally got around to handle this.  See #13994.
